title: Luxury Vinyl Plank vs Hardwood: Honest Pros and Cons for Snohomish Homeowners
meta: LVP vs hardwood for Snohomish homes: honest pros, cons and 20-year costs from Wills Flooring, with $2.50 and $3.25 per sq ft install labor and a calculator.
keywords: luxury vinyl plank vs hardwood, LVP vs hardwood pros and cons, vinyl plank or hardwood flooring, is LVP better than hardwood, hardwood vs LVP cost, Snohomish WA flooring

blocks.lead: For a Snohomish house with dogs, mud, a crawlspace and a wood stove, luxury vinyl plank is the practical winner. Hardwood is the better long-term asset if you plan to stay 15 or more years, can keep standing water off it, and care about resale on a larger property.
blocks.detail: Wills Flooring installs both, LVP at $2.50 per sq ft and hardwood at $3.25 per sq ft for labor, with material quoted separately. Neither is the cheap option or the fancy option anymore. Here are the real trade-offs, including the ones that do not fit on a showroom sign.

blocks.html: Snohomish is where this debate gets honest. Out on acreage in Clearview or up Fobes Hill, the floor takes wet dogs, muck boots, firewood splinters and the dry heat of a wood stove all winter. Downtown, a Victorian with original fir raises a different question: cover it with plank, or restore it? We have installed both floors in both kinds of houses for over a decade, and the right answer follows the house, not the trend.

items.title: What vinyl plank does well
items.text: Waterproof through the core, so a dog bowl, a leaking fridge line or a tracked-in puddle is a non-event. Quiet and slightly soft underfoot. Rigid SPC cores resist dents. Installs fast, floats over most existing floors, and costs less in labor and usually in material. Twenty-mil wear layers shrug off claws well.

items.title: Where it falls short
items.text: It cannot be refinished; when the wear layer is gone, the floor is done. Repeating patterns can look artificial in big open rooms. It expands in heat and can peak near a wood stove or south slider if the gaps are wrong. Rural buyers and appraisers still price it below real wood.

items.title: What hardwood does well
items.text: Real wood ages instead of wearing out: scratches become character, and a sanding every 15 to 20 years makes it new again. Solid oak lasts a century. It carries resale weight, especially on the larger Snohomish properties where buyers expect a certain finish level. Species like hickory and white oak stand up to dogs better than their reputation.

items.title: Where it falls short
items.text: Water is the enemy: a slow leak or a wet crawlspace cups it. It costs more in labor and usually in material, and refinishing is a multi-day disruption. A wood stove drying the house to 20 percent humidity opens gaps. Large dogs will scratch a soft species or a glossy finish.

blocks.text: Snohomish factors that tip the decision

items.html: Crawlspace moisture. Most homes outside downtown sit over a vented crawlspace. If it runs wet, hardwood needs a vapor retarder and a dry season to acclimate. LVP does not care, but the subfloor under it still should be dry.
Wood stove heat. Stoves pull indoor humidity down hard. Solid hardwood gaps; engineered moves less; LVP is stable but needs its expansion gap near the hearth.
Dogs and mud. Two farm dogs in and out all winter is the strongest argument for LVP we know. If you still want wood, choose hickory or white oak with a matte finish and mats at every door.
Well water and softeners. Softener brine and iron-rich well water mark both floors; hardwood needs the spill wiped quickly, LVP just wipes.
Historic downtown houses. If a Victorian or farmhouse has original fir, refinishing it at $3.99 per sq ft usually beats covering it with plank, both for cost and for what buyers will pay later.
The rural resale market. On acreage and higher-end properties, buyers still read hardwood as a signal. In a starter home or rental, plank is fully accepted.

a.title: Choose LVP when
items: Large dogs, kids, mud and a busy entry
Slab, daylight basement or a damp crawlspace
You want one floor from mudroom to great room for less
You may move within 10 to 15 years

b.title: Choose hardwood when
items: You plan to stay 15 or more years
The house is historic or upper-market and buyers will expect it
You can keep water off it and humidity stable
You like the idea of refinishing instead of replacing

blocks.title: Do not pick LVP because you think hardwood cannot handle dogs:
blocks.text: It can, with the right species and a matte finish. Pick LVP because you have water, a slab, a budget or a timeline. Those are the honest reasons. Our hardwood for dogs guide covers the species question.

items.html: Check what is under the carpet. Original fir or oak changes the whole math.
Get the crawlspace and subfloor moisture read. We do it at the estimate, and it rules hardwood in or out fast.
Compare specs, not slogans. Wear layer in mils for LVP; species, wear layer and finish for hardwood.
Get both priced on one sheet. Labor is published on our price list; material is the variable, and you should see it for each option.
Ask who stands behind it. Every Wills Flooring install carries a 1-year workmanship warranty, and our Lynnwood showroom is 25 minutes from Snohomish when something needs a look.

faq.q: Is luxury vinyl plank better than hardwood?
faq.a: Neither is better across the board. LVP is better for water, pets, slabs and budgets, and it needs no refinishing. Hardwood is better for longevity, resale and the ability to renew the floor by sanding. In Snohomish, the house, the dogs and how long you are staying usually make the choice for you.

faq.q: Does LVP lower home value compared to hardwood?
faq.a: It does not lower value, but it does not add what hardwood adds. In starter homes and rentals, quality plank is fully accepted. On acreage and in historic or higher-priced Snohomish homes, buyers and appraisers still give hardwood a premium. Cheap, thin plank with visible wear can hurt a listing.

faq.q: How much cheaper is LVP than hardwood to install?
faq.a: At Wills Flooring the labor is $2.50 per sq ft for vinyl plank and $3.25 for hardwood, so on 1,000 sq ft that is $2,500 versus $3,250. Material widens the gap, since comparable-quality plank usually costs less per box than hardwood. Both have a 500 sq ft minimum.

faq.q: Which is better for dogs, LVP or hardwood?
faq.a: For accidents and wet paws, LVP wins clearly. For claws, a 20 mil LVP and a matte-finished hickory or white oak perform similarly, and both beat a soft or glossy hardwood. If your dogs come in from the field twice a day, LVP is the safer choice; a well-chosen hardwood is not a mistake.

faq.q: Can LVP go near a wood stove?
faq.a: Yes, with care. Vinyl plank is stable, but it expands with heat, so it needs its full expansion gap at the hearth and walls and should not be installed under the stove itself. Radiant heat from a stove on a floating plank floor within a foot or two can soften it; a hearth pad solves that.

faq.q: How long does each floor last?
faq.a: Quality LVP with a 20 mil wear layer lasts 15 to 25 years in a busy home and is then replaced. Solid hardwood lasts 80 to 100 years with a refinish every 15 to 20 years; engineered hardwood 30 to 60 depending on wear layer thickness. Over one ownership, they often cost about the same.
